artworks.title: Achilles Fighting the River Gods Xanthus and Simois
artworks.description: Couder's Louvre decoration names both Trojan rivers — Simois beside Scamander (Xanthus) rising against Achilles in Iliad XXI.

artworks.title: Achilles Fighting Scamander and Simois
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print: Achilles locked with both river-gods — Simois as Scamander's partner in the flood that almost drowns the hero.

artworks.title: Achilles in Combat with Scamander and Simois
artworks.description: Another Rijksmuseum plate of the double river battle — Simois named in the title as Troy's second watery foe.

artworks.title: The Simoeis Plain
artworks.description: Clarke's travel view of the Simoeis plain in the Troad — the mortal landscape of the river-god who fought beside Scamander.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book XXI — Simois answers Scamander's call and joins the flood against Achilles until Hephaestus' fire drives the rivers back.

popCulture.title: Simoeis
popCulture.description: God of Troy's second river — Scamander's ally in the Iliad's river battle, and a name still on the Troad map.
